reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the finding correctly proposes no redline and no counterparty comment, which is the expected output for a compliant classification.

The cited text substantively covers the rule's material terms in our favour: Section 14.3.1/11.1.1.4 transfer ownership of the Trial Data Package and Research Results to PB on any termination; 14.3.3 requires delivery of complete copies of Product Filings; 14.3.4 provides for wind-down or transfer of control plus continued conduct of the Clinical Trials for a transition period; 14.3.5 assigns CRO/Vendor/Clinical Trial Agreements with good-faith transition cooperation; 3.11.1 gives PB copies of all Clinical Trial data, CRFs and the Master File on request; and 10.3 provides return-or-destroy of Confidential Information with written officer certification (the certified-deletion element).

The failed deterministic regex ('data return/transition present') is explained by domain phrasing — this pharma co-development agreement uses assignment/delivery/transfer-of-control and CRF/Master File language rather than SaaS-style 'transition services' or 'data export' wording — so it is a phrasing variant, not evidence of absence.

Shortfalls identified (redacted [***] delivery and trial-continuation periods, no 'machine-readable format' standard) are correctly treated as rationale notes rather than independent deviations under the playbook's minor sub-element guidance, and the rationale flags the practical diligence point (confirm the redacted periods are at least 30/90 days).
Rationale is accurate to the quoted paragraphs; no misattribution of obligations or overstatement of what the clauses provide.
